== History ==
The year of the shrine's founding is unknown. The current shrine building was constructed in {{ill|1720|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} 5).

The shrine was highly revered by the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|de|Hachisuka (Klan)|fa|خاندان هاچیسوکا|fr|Clan Hachisuka|hu|Hacsiszuka család|id|Klan Hachisuka|it|Clan Hachisuka|ja|蜂須賀氏|pt|Clã Hachisuka|ru|Хатисука (род)|zh|蜂須賀氏|qid=Q2975261}}, feudal lords of the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|es|Dominio de Tokushima|fa|قلمرو توکوشیما|fr|Domaine de Tokushima|ja|徳島藩|ko|도쿠시마번|ru|Токусима (княжество)|uk|Токушіма-хан|zh|德島藩|qid=Q3034557}}. During its annual grand festival, members of the clan would often personally visit or send representatives. In {{ill|1627|es|Kan'ei|fa|کانئی|fr|Ère Kan'ei|id|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|ko|간에이|ru|Канъэй|simple|Kan'ei|sr|Канеи|sv|Kanei|tr|Kan'ei|zh|寬永|qid=Q1192913}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|es|Kan'ei|fa|کانئی|fr|Ère Kan'ei|id|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|ko|간에이|ru|Канъэй|simple|Kan'ei|sr|Канеи|sv|Kanei|tr|Kan'ei|zh|寬永|qid=Q1192913}} 4), {{ill|Hachisuka Mitsutaka|fr|Hachisuka Mitsutaka|ja|蜂須賀光隆|qid=Q3125458}} prayed at the shrine and reported miraculous occurrences. Additionally, because visits by the Hachisuka could be blocked by flooding of the {{ill|Akui River|ceb|Akui Gawa|ja|鮎喰川|qid=Q11674107}}, a division of the shrine's spirit was transferred to {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|qid=Q11631927}} near {{ill|Tokushima Castle|de|Burg Tokushima|es|Castillo de Tokushima|fr|Château de Tokushima|ja|徳島城|ko|도쿠시마성|ml|ടോകുഷിമ കാസിൽ|zh|德島城|qid=Q8011246}} for easier access during times when flooding prevented direct visits to Take Minato Jinja.

According to the shrine's historical records (''Ura-shō Village History''), "In the tenth year of {{ill|Hōki|de|Hōki (Ära)|es|Hōki (nengō)|fa|هوکی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hōki|ia|Hoki (era)|id|Hōki|ja|宝亀|ko|호키 (연호)|pt|Hōki (era)|ru|Хоки (нэнго)|simple|Hōki|sr|Хоки|tr|Hōki|uk|Хокі|zh|寶龜|zh_yue|寶龜|qid=Q18520676}} during the reign of Emperor {{ill|Kōnin|ar|الإمبراطور كونين|arz|الامبراطور كونين|azb|کونین (ایمپیراتور)|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆنین|cs|Kónin|de|Kōnin|es|Kōnin Tennō|eu|Kōnin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور کونین|fi|Kōnin|fr|Kōnin|hu|Kónin japán császár|id|Kaisar Kōnin|it|Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇|ko|고닌 천황|mn|Эзэн Хаан Коонин|mr|कोनिन|nl|Konin (keizer)|pl|Kōnin|pt|Konin|ru|Император Конин|sh|Car Kōnin|simple|Emperor Kōnin|sl|Cesar Konin|sv|Kōnin|th|จักรพรรดิโคนิง|tl|Emperador Kōnin|tr|Kōnin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Конін|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōnin|yo|Emperor Kōnin|zh|光仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Kônin Thian-hông|qid=Q958662}} (779 CE), the Suwa Daimyōjin of Nakata District, Awa Province, was transferred and enshrined at the Minato This implies that {{ill|Takeminakata no Mikoto|ja|建御名方命}}, known for his mythological dispute with {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武御雷神}} in the kuni-yuzuri episode, originally hailed from Awa Province, and that Suwa Taisha's origins trace back to Awa, as recorded in the shrine's documents.<ref>Sasada Takashi, *The Imperial Capital Yamato was Awa*, Sun Lotus Research Institute, 2024, pp. 173-185.</ref>

== Access ==
* Approximately a 25-minute walk from {{ill|Shimoura Station|ja|下浦駅|ko|시모우라역|ur|شیمورا اسٹیشن|zh|下浦站|qid=Q7497021}} on the {{ill|Tokushima Line|fr|Ligne Tokushima|id|Jalur Tokushima|it|Linea Tokushima|ja|徳島線|ko|도쿠시마선|zh|德島線|qid=Q899310}} ({{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|ca|Companyia de Ferrocarrils de Shikoku|cs|JR Šikoku|de|Shikoku Railway Company|es|JR Shikoku|fa|راه‌آهن شیکوکو|fi|JR Shikoku|fr|Shikoku Railway Company|hu|Shikoku Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Kereta Api Shikoku|it|Shikoku Railway Company|ja|四国旅客鉄道|jv|Shikoku Railway Company|ko|시코쿠 여객철도|nds|JR Shikoku|pt|Shikoku Railway Company|ru|Shikoku Railway Company|tr|Shikoku Railway Company|wuu|四国旅客铁道|zh|四國旅客鐵道|zh_yue|四國旅客鐵道|qid=Q496531|lt=JR Shikoku}}).
* Approximately a 20-minute walk from {{ill|Ushijima Station|ja|牛島駅|ko|우시노시마역|ur|اوشینوشیما اسٹیشن|zh|牛島站|qid=Q11570130}} on the same line.

== History ==
The founding year is unknown. It was deeply revered by the Hachisuka family, lords of the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|es|Dominio de Tokushima|fa|قلمرو توکوشیما|fr|Domaine de Tokushima|ja|徳島藩|ko|도쿠시마번|ru|Токусима (княжество)|uk|Токушіма-хан|zh|德島藩|qid=Q3034557}}, who worshiped in person or by proxy at the annual grand festival. In {{ill|1627|ab|1627|af|1627|als|1627|am|1627 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1627|ar|1627|ary|1627|arz|1627|ast|1627|avk|1627|az|1627|azb|۱۶۲۷ (میلادی)|ban|1627|bar|1627|bcl|1627|be|1627|be_x_old|1627|bg|1627|bn|১৬২৭|bpy|মারি ১৬২৭|br|1627|bs|1627.|ca|1627|cdo|1627 nièng|ceb|1627|ckb|١٦٢٧|co|1627|crh|1627|cs|1627|cv|1627|cy|1627|da|1627|de|1627|diq|1627|el|1627|eml|1627|eo|1627|es|1627|et|1627|eu|1627|fa|۱۶۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|1627|fo|1627|fr|1627|frr|1627|fur|1627|fy|1627|ga|1627|gan|1627年|gcr|1627|gd|1627|gl|1627|gn|1627|gv|1627|he|1627|hi|१६२७|hif|1627|hr|1627.|ht|1627 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1627|hy|1627|hyw|1627 թուական|ia|1627|id|1627|ilo|1627|io|1627|is|1627|it|1627|ja|1627年|jbo|1627moi|jv|1627|ka|1627|kaa|1627|kk|1627 жыл|kn|೧೬೨೭|ko|1627년|krc|1627 джыл|la|1627|lb|1627|lez|1627 йис|li|1627|lij|1627|lmo|1627|lt|1627 m.|lv|1627. gads|mai|१६२७|map_bms|1627|mdf|1627|mg|1627|mhr|1627|mi|1627|mk|1627|mr|इ.स. १६२७|mrj|1627 и|ms|1627|my|၁၆၂၇|mzn|۱۶۲۷|nap|1627|nds|1627|nds_nl|1627|new|सन् १६२७|nl|1627|nn|1627|no|1627|nov|1627|nrm|1627|nso|1627|oc|1627|or|୧୬୨୭|os|1627-æм аз|pa|1627|pl|1627|pnb|1627|pt|1627|qu|1627|ro|1627|ru|1627 год|rue|1627|sa|१६२७|sah|1627|sc|1627|scn|1627|sd|1627ع|se|1627|sh|1627.|shn|1627|simple|1627|sk|1627|sl|1627|smn|1627|sq|1627|sr|1627|su|1627|sv|1627|sw|1627|szl|1627|ta|1627|te|1627|tg|Соли 1627|th|พ.ศ. 2170|tk|1627|tl|1627|tly|1627|tr|1627|tt|1627 ел|uk|1627|ur|1627ء|uz|1627|vec|1627|vi|1627|vls|1627|wa|1627|war|1627|wuu|1627年|xmf|1627|yi|1627|zh|1627年|zh_min_nan|1627 nî|zh_yue|1627年|qid=Q6833}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|es|Kan'ei|fa|کانئی|fr|Ère Kan'ei|id|Kan'ei|ja|寛永|ko|간에이|ru|Канъэй|simple|Kan'ei|sr|Канеи|sv|Kanei|tr|Kan'ei|zh|寬永|qid=Q1192913}} 4), {{ill|Hachisuka Mitsutaka|fr|Hachisuka Mitsutaka|ja|蜂須賀光隆|qid=Q3125458}} prayed and reportedly received auspicious signs. It is also said that because visits by the Hachisuka could be blocked by flooding of the {{ill|Akui River|ceb|Akui Gawa|ja|鮎喰川|qid=Q11674107}}, a divided spirit was enshrined at {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|qid=Q11631927|lt=Suwa Shrine}} near {{ill|Tokushima Castle|de|Burg Tokushima|es|Castillo de Tokushima|fr|Château de Tokushima|ja|徳島城|ko|도쿠시마성|ml|ടോകുഷിമ കാസിൽ|zh|德島城|qid=Q8011246}}.

In other words, this record preserves a view that the original base of Takeminakata, who contended with {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|it|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|kk|Такэмикадзути|ko|타케미카즈치|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|tr|Takemikazuchi|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi}} in the kuni-yuzuri episode, was in Awa, and that Suwa Taisha in Nagano was invited from Awa after the compilation of the Kiki<ref>Sasada Takashi, ''The Imperial Capital Yamato Was Awa'', Sun Lotus Research Institute, 2024, pp.173-185.</ref>.
